buoyancy.d.rhoO: Density of the object (a cube). Cork about 240, wood about 600, ice 917, aluminium 2700, iron 7870 kg/m³
buoyancy.d.rhoF: Density of the fluid (when the fluid in the settings is 'Slider value')
buoyancy.d.fluid: Kind of fluid. A named fluid sets its density and hides the $\rho_f$ slider
buoyancy.d.a: Side length of the cube (changing it restarts)
buoyancy.d.press: Arrows for the fluid pressure (gauge, $\rho_f g d$) pushing on the top and bottom faces
buoyancy.goal.arch: Archimedes' principle: the buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced fluid, $F_b = \rho_f V_\text{sub}\, g$. It comes from the pressure difference between the bottom and top faces, $F_b = (p_\text{bot} - p_\text{top})A$
buoyancy.goal.float: Float or sink: for $\rho_\text{obj} < \rho_f$ the object floats with $V_\text{sub}/V = \rho_\text{obj}/\rho_f$ submerged; for $\rho_\text{obj} > \rho_f$ it sinks
buoyancy.obs.drag: Drag the block up or down and let go: it bobs and comes to rest at the depth where $F_b = F_g$. The dashed line in the plot is $\rho_\text{obj}/\rho_f$
buoyancy.obs.frac: Wood (600 kg/m³) floats 0.60 submerged in water. Ice (917 kg/m³) floats 0.917 submerged in water and 0.895 in sea water
buoyancy.obs.sink: $\rho_\text{obj} > \rho_f$: the block sinks to the floor, which pushes up with the normal force $N = F_g - F_b$. Once fully submerged, the buoyant force no longer depends on depth
buoyancy.obs.press: Grey arrows: gauge pressure $\rho_f g d$ on the top and bottom faces. The bottom face is deeper, so its pressure is larger; the net upward pressure force is the buoyant force. Pressures on the side faces cancel
buoyancy.obs.level: Fluid level: it rises by the submerged volume over the tank area, $\Delta h = V_\text{sub}/A_t$. The short dashed line $h_0$ is the level without the block
buoyancy.obs.fluid: Mercury (13600 kg/m³): even iron (7870 kg/m³) floats, 0.58 submerged
buoyancy.obs.period: Period of small bobbing $T = 2\pi\sqrt{(d_\text{eq}/g)(1 - A/A_t)}$, with $d_\text{eq}$ the submerged depth at equilibrium. Wood 600 kg/m³, $a$ = 0.20 m, water: $T$ = 0.67 s
buoyancy.as.tank: Tank: inner cross-section 0.8 m × 0.8 m ($A_t$ = 0.64 m²), fluid depth without the block $h_0$ = 0.40 m. The fluid volume is fixed, so the level rise is part of the calculation
buoyancy.as.damp: Damping: a linear drag $F_d = -bv$ while the block is in the fluid, with $b$ set for a damping ratio $\zeta$ = 0.05 of small bobbing (the amplitude drops by about 27 % per period). No air drag
buoyancy.as.fluid: Fluid inertia (added mass), waves and surface tension are neglected. The block moves only vertically and does not tilt. $g = 9.81\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. The atmospheric pressure $p_0$ adds equally to the top and bottom faces and cancels, so arrows and formulas use gauge pressure
buoyancy.as.floor: A thin fluid film is assumed under a block resting on the floor (the bottom-face pressure stays). The collision with the floor is perfectly inelastic
buoyancy.as.arrows: Force arrows share a linear scale (set by the larger of $F_g$ and the largest buoyant force of free bobbing). The large buoyant force on a light block pushed deep is cut at 1.8 times that length. $F_g$ acts at the centre of mass (black dot), $F_b$ at the centre of buoyancy, the centre of the submerged part (open circle); they are drawn slightly apart so they do not cover each other. Hatching: the submerged volume $V_\text{sub}$
